summary:
RotaTerra is an agricultural decision-support platform that helps farmers make sustainable decisions about what and when to grow their crops. Bringing together historical climate data from NASA POWER, along with soil data from SoilGrids, it helps to build a picture of the farm's environmental conditions, considering a multitude of factors, such as rainfall, temperature and soil composition. Using this information, RotaTerra compares local conditions with the requirements of different crops to assess suitability, both economically and environmentally.

However, the platform goes beyond simple suggestions. It offers a rotation planner, where it ranks multi-season crop sequences, taking into account multiple factors like economic potential, crop diversity and soil health. It also considers how changing climate conditions could affect the suitability of crops in the future, aiding the farmer in building long-term resilience. 

By bringing together real environmental data and science, we aim to make complicated farming decisions easier and more accessible, supporting more resource-efficient and sustainable-driven agriculture.
details:
RotaTerra is a free, browser-based decision-support tool that helps farmers decide what to grow and in what order. The farmer enters their farm’s latitude and longitude. The app then retrieves 25 years (2000-2024) of NASA POWER data on rainfall, temperature and solar radiation, plus soil data (sand, clay and organic carbon) from ISRIC SoilGrids for that exact spot.

It estimates how much water crops would need using temperature and latitude (Hargreaves-Samani evapotranspiration, following FAO-56). It then scores 17 crops from 0 to 100 on temperature, rainfall, sunlight, soil and water balance, testing every possible planting month and keeping each crop’s best window. Next, it searches thousands of 3-, 4- and 5-season crop sequences and ranks the best ones on crop fit, soil health, crop-family variety, water balance, pest and disease breaks, and economic value. Every result comes with a plain-language explanation. A final page re-scores the rotations under warmer, drier “what if” conditions to show which plans are fragile, and a printable report pulls everything together.

Intended Impact

Most crop advice looks at one crop at a time. RotaTerra looks at the whole sequence, because what grows this season affects the soil, the pests and the water available in later seasons. It makes NASA Earth observation data usable by people without a scientific background, with no account, install or cost. We hope it helps farmers, especially smallholders with limited access to an agronomist, make more informed, sustainable and climate-aware planting decisions.

Tools and technology

  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript (ES modules), with no framework or build step
  • NASA POWER API (climate data) and ISRIC SoilGrids REST API (soil data)

How it is creative

The core idea is to score entire rotations rather than single crops. The app turns complex results into farmer-friendly output: ratings in words, colour-coded season blocks in the rotation plan, a “how to use this page” guide on every screen, and one-click example farms. The scoring is transparent and adjustable, and the app documents its own method and limits on a “How it works” page. It also never invents data. When a source is unavailable, it says so and leaves that factor out of the score.

Factors we considered

  • Honesty. Scores show how well a crop fits local conditions. They are not yield predictions, and the app says so. Observed data and what-if scenarios are kept clearly separate.
  • Accessibility. Plain language, a mobile-friendly layout and no sign-up.
  • Transparency. Adjustable weights, documented formulas and unit tests for the maths.
dataRefs: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources). Used monthly point data API from 2000 to 2024.
projectRefs: ISRIC SoilGrids (global soil properties) accessed by its REST API.
